items.summary: This artifact accompanies “Normal Forms and Complete Relations for Circuits in Agda” (POPL 2027 paper #911), by Xiaoning Bian and Yuan Feng. This version combines the source code and the linked Agda HTML rendering in one archive, acir-popl-revision2.zip. Extract the entire archive; the top-level acir-popl-revision2 directory contains the Agda sources, README.md, LICENSE.txt, the revised paper sources, and the html/ folder. No separate HTML download is needed. Browse without installing Agda: open html/index.html in a web browser, follow the MainTheorems entry point, and click identifiers to jump to their definitions. All links and styling are local, so the rendering works offline. The html/ folder contains 422 generated module pages: MainTheorems and its transitive imports, including 61 artifact modules and the required Agda built-in and standard-library modules. It does not render every unused repository module. To typecheck the source, read the top-level README.md and run agda MainTheorems.agda using Agda 2.8.0 and Agda standard library 2.4. To regenerate the HTML from the repository root, run: agda --html --html-dir=html MainTheorems.agda. The rendering was generated and typechecked on October 25, 2026. All 306,902 local file links and anchors were checked with no broken targets. The html/README.txt file provides viewing, regeneration, provenance, and license information. The Agda sources are unchanged from the popl-revision1 release, commit 5e28af3f344c11b27096c012c2f7b7be4cc51bf5. Dependency notices are preserved in html/AGDA-LICENSE.txt, html/AGDA-STDLIB-LICENSE.txt, and the rendered sources. The paper manuscript, paper sources, slides, and other publication materials are excluded from this MIT license grant. items.summary: Runtime query similarity identification supports several activities, including workload analysis, identifying recurring behaviour, auditing, debugging, and anomaly detection. Existing methods for evaluating query similarity mostly rely on SQL text, execution plans, or result values but do not account for input data or how results are derived during query execution. This paper proposes a novel approach using data provenance for query-template identification. We construct query-level profiles that capture explicit data dependencies, occurrence frequencies, and structural properties by aggregating tuple-level Lineage and Why-provenance across entire query results. We also derive Provenance Structural Descriptors (PSD), which summarise these profiles using a small set of numerical features. We evaluate our proposals using these profiles to identify query templates over \(12{,}500\) distinct query instances generated from parametrised TPC-DS query templates. The experimental evaluation shows that query templates can be identified solely from their provenance footprints, and that accuracy improves as more historical data becomes available. It also shows that PSD achieve high classification accuracy with limited training history and low test-processing cost.
items.title: Data Provenance Aggregation and Structural Descriptors for Query-Template Identification

items.summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
items.title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

items.summary: This deposit contains the model code, the complete parameter set with provenance labels, all numerical outputs, and the scripts required to regenerate every figure and table in the associated manuscript. The work is a physiologically based kinetic (PBK) analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin, an anthraquinone of rhubarb. The model is an eight-compartment, perfusion-limited PBK model with intestinal and hepatic first-pass metabolism, biliary excretion and enterohepatic recirculation, parameterised for mouse, rat and human. No experimental data were generated: the study is entirely computational. The published pharmacokinetic data used for calibration and external validation are cited in the manuscript; the extracted values are recorded in results/validation_split.csv. The absorption term was calibrated against four published rat plasma datasets, and the fitted value with all residuals is included. Code is additionally available under the MIT licence (see LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures are released under CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Data and code for: A physiologically based kinetic analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin

items.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are increasingly deployed through black-box APIs and trained on large collections of real-world tabular datasets. As this training paradigm becomes more widely adopted, private or proprietary datasets may be incorporated into pre-training corpora, yet there are currently no dedicated methods for determining whether a given tabular dataset was used to train a TFM. As a solution, we introduce the first dataset inference method for TFMs, aiming to infer whether a suspect dataset was part of a model's pre-training data. We systematically analyze a broad collection of candidate signals that can be observed from a black-box TFM via input manipulation and find that individual signals provide only weak evidence of training data membership. However, by combining multiple complementary signals, we can infer dataset membership for several state-of-the-art TFMs trained on real tabular data, achieving up to 0.99 ROCAUC dependent on the TFM. We then study factors that influence dataset identification, including pre-training data composition, model capacity, and the use of real vs. synthetic data. Our results show that our dataset inference method is a practical auditing tool for detecting privacy leakage and the use of proprietary datasets in TFMs.
items.title: Dataset Inference for Data Provenance and Privacy Auditing in Tabular Foundation Models

items.summary: Multimodal $ΔΔG$ predictors integrating protein language models with inverse-folding representations achieve strong in-distribution accuracy on the Megascale dataset but exhibit limited robustness on out-of-distribution (OOD) proteins, persistent forward-reverse bias on paired-mutation benchmarks, and under-representation of rare stabilizing mutations. Existing approaches address these limitations primarily through additional architectural components, leaving optimization-level intervention comparatively underexplored. We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. Across eleven benchmarks and three random seeds, the framework improves Spearman correlation on S669 from 0.486 to 0.540 ($σ=0.002$ across seeds), matching the published SPURS baseline (0.50) without architectural modification, and on S461 from 0.653 to 0.711, with consistent smaller gains on five additional OOD datasets. A controlled diagnostic on Ssym reveals that anti-symmetric training does not eliminate systematic forward-reverse bias, indicating that gains arise through implicit regularization rather than exact thermodynamic constraint enforcement.
items.title: Constraint-Aware Optimization for Robust Protein Stability Prediction

Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
items.title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

items.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are increasingly deployed through black-box APIs and trained on large collections of real-world tabular datasets. As this training paradigm becomes more widely adopted, private or proprietary datasets may be incorporated into pre-training corpora, yet there are currently no dedicated methods for determining whether a given tabular dataset was used to train a TFM. As a solution, we introduce the first dataset inference method for TFMs, aiming to infer whether a suspect dataset was part of a model's pre-training data. We systematically analyze a broad collection of candidate signals that can be observed from a black-box TFM via input manipulation and find that individual signals provide only weak evidence of training data membership. However, by combining multiple complementary signals, we can infer dataset membership for several state-of-the-art TFMs trained on real tabular data, achieving up to 0.99 ROCAUC dependent on the TFM. We then study factors that influence dataset identification, including pre-training data composition, model capacity, and the use of real vs. synthetic data. Our results show that our dataset inference method is a practical auditing tool for detecting privacy leakage and the use of proprietary datasets in TFMs.
items.title: Dataset Inference for Data Provenance and Privacy Auditing in Tabular Foundation Models

items.summary: This artifact accompanies “Normal Forms and Complete Relations for Circuits in Agda” (POPL 2027 paper #911), by Xiaoning Bian and Yuan Feng. This version combines the source code and the linked Agda HTML rendering in one archive, acir-popl-revision2.zip. Extract the entire archive; the top-level acir-popl-revision2 directory contains the Agda sources, README.md, LICENSE.txt, the revised paper sources, and the html/ folder. No separate HTML download is needed. Browse without installing Agda: open html/index.html in a web browser, follow the MainTheorems entry point, and click identifiers to jump to their definitions. All links and styling are local, so the rendering works offline. The html/ folder contains 422 generated module pages: MainTheorems and its transitive imports, including 61 artifact modules and the required Agda built-in and standard-library modules. It does not render every unused repository module. To typecheck the source, read the top-level README.md and run agda MainTheorems.agda using Agda 2.8.0 and Agda standard library 2.4. To regenerate the HTML from the repository root, run: agda --html --html-dir=html MainTheorems.agda. The rendering was generated and typechecked on October 25, 2026. All 306,902 local file links and anchors were checked with no broken targets. The html/README.txt file provides viewing, regeneration, provenance, and license information. The Agda sources are unchanged from the popl-revision1 release, commit 5e28af3f344c11b27096c012c2f7b7be4cc51bf5. This combined version also contains the revised paper sources and updated documentation from the popl-revision2 branch. Build/test environment: Intel Core i5-14400 x86-64 PC (16 logical processors), 16 GB RAM, Linux under WSL version 2.7.12.0 on Windows 11 25H2. License: the artifact software and accompanying software documentation are released under the MIT License; see the top-level LICENSE.txt for scope. Dependency notices are preserved in html/AGDA-LICENSE.txt, html/AGDA-STDLIB-LICENSE.txt, and the rendered sources. The paper manuscript, paper sources, slides, and other publication materials are excluded from this MIT license grant. Repository: https://github.com/onestruggler/acir/tree/popl-revision2   Archived Git commit: 391edbaad08e6c5427875da2ea7b7eaa973d6122 (https://github.com/onestruggler/acir/tree/391edbaad08e6c5427875da2ea7b7eaa973d6122).

items.summary: This record accompanies the manuscript “Feedback Leakage in Historical Continuous Integration Test-Selection Evaluation”. It contains author-created replay and analysis code, frozen protocol descriptions, aggregate experimental results, figure source data, portable plotting scripts, provenance records, and verification information. The materials cover the industrial feedback comparison, first-failure and statistical analyses, exploratory adaptive reserve, recorded-cost analyses, and bounded external/reconstruction studies. Third-party raw archives, normalized input rows, and per-action selected test or row identities are excluded. Source locations, versions, hashes, and access conditions are documented so that permitted inputs can be obtained separately. The package supports two levels of reproduction: (1) computations that can be directly reproduced using the included summaries, and (2) selection replays that require separately obtained external inputs. It does not claim to provide a self-contained, one-click rerun for every historical execution. Author-created code is licensed under MIT. Original aggregate results, figures, and documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials are excluded from these author grants and remain subject to their original terms. Three unmodified figure-audit helpers retain their upstream Apache-2.0 licence and attribution; see LICENSE_SCOPE.md and SOURCES_AND_THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE.md.
items.title: Replication materials for Feedback Leakage in Historical Continuous Integration Test-Selection Evaluation

items.summary: Multimodal $ΔΔG$ predictors integrating protein language models with inverse-folding representations achieve strong in-distribution accuracy on the Megascale dataset but exhibit limited robustness on out-of-distribution (OOD) proteins, persistent forward-reverse bias on paired-mutation benchmarks, and under-representation of rare stabilizing mutations. Existing approaches address these limitations primarily through additional architectural components, leaving optimization-level intervention comparatively underexplored. We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. Across eleven benchmarks and three random seeds, the framework improves Spearman correlation on S669 from 0.486 to 0.540 ($σ=0.002$ across seeds), matching the published SPURS baseline (0.50) without architectural modification, and on S461 from 0.653 to 0.711, with consistent smaller gains on five additional OOD datasets. A controlled diagnostic on Ssym reveals that anti-symmetric training does not eliminate systematic forward-reverse bias, indicating that gains arise through implicit regularization rather than exact thermodynamic constraint enforcement.
items.title: Constraint-Aware Optimization for Robust Protein Stability Prediction

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.
items.title: A Caputo Fractional-Order Optimal Control Framework for NdFeB Permanent Magnet Supply-Chain Resilience under Recycling Delay and Geopolitical Risk

items.summary: This deposit contains the model code, the complete parameter set with provenance labels, all numerical outputs, and the scripts required to regenerate every figure and table in the associated manuscript. The work is a physiologically based kinetic (PBK) analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin, an anthraquinone of rhubarb. The model is an eight-compartment, perfusion-limited PBK model with intestinal and hepatic first-pass metabolism, biliary excretion and enterohepatic recirculation, parameterised for mouse, rat and human. No experimental data were generated: the study is entirely computational. The published pharmacokinetic data used for calibration and external validation are cited in the manuscript; the extracted values are recorded in results/validation_split.csv. The absorption term was calibrated against four published rat plasma datasets, and the fitted value with all residuals is included. Code is additionally available under the MIT licence (see LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures are released under CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Data and code for: A physiologically based kinetic analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin

items.summary: We study full-cohort change in two binary latent states observed through a shared, incompletely calibrated anchor and a second item whose channel may change between waves. All baseline items are observed; follow-up response depends only on the follow-up latent state, with a bounded selection odds ratio. The input is the entire twenty-cell observed law. A nonzero respondent cross-wave anchor covariance gives point identification through classical three-view and shadow-variable mechanisms. At zero covariance the latent transition has rank one. We eliminate the drifting channels, obtain the exact feasible rectangle for the common anchor, and show that one corner realizes the complete set of possible signs of latent change. This yields an explicit sharp selection threshold. A positive-probability example has identical observed laws and opposite changes; full-rank perturbations approach this law while retaining a fixed target gap. The results are conditional population-law calculations with external calibration inputs.
items.title: Sharp directions of change at a rank boundary in a two-wave binary measurement model

items.summary: Added Animations as GIF : Export GIF... in the animation bar (or Fields > Export Animation as GIF...) saves all frames of the running animation as a looping GIF. Each frame is the view exactly as shown, in its pixel size, and the GIF runs at the speed you see: the bar measures the frames per second actually drawn during playback (shown next to the speed setting, it can be lower than the setting for heavy plots) and the GIF uses that rate. Without a measurement the export first plays the animation for a moment to measure it. All frames share one colour palette, so the colour scale and the field do not change colour from frame to frame. Object groups : Edit > Group (Ctrl+G) puts the selected objects, also solids, sheets and lines together, into one group. A click on a member in the 3D view selects the whole group, so Move, Rotate, Mirror, Copy, Hide or Delete act on all of it; the model tree lists the groups under Groups (rename, ungroup, single members selectable there). Edit > Ungroup (Ctrl+Shift+G) dissolves a group to edit single objects again. Groups are saved in the project. SMD components (C, L, R, Touchstone parts) are inserted as a group of pads, terminations and element sheet, and the integration line of a lumped port or element now moves with its objects. Box selection in the 3D view : a left drag draws a rectangle and selects every object that lies completely inside it (in face, edge or vertex mode: every face, edge or vertex completely inside). Ctrl + drag adds to the selection. A group is selected only when all its members are inside. Hidden objects are skipped; a click still selects one item. Mesh refinement "AURA (EMerge)" , EMerge's own local refinement, with the same error estimate, convergence criterion and curved elements as the other methods. A comparison script measures the time to solution against Local (Delaunay) on the benchmark models ( examples/benchmark/mesher ). Lumped Elements tab : inserts a chip resistor, inductor or capacitor, or a component measured by a Touchstone file: pick the package in the menu of the button and click the position on the board. The part comes with its pads (Perfect E), and its position is the design variables <name>_x/_y/_z, so it moves as a whole. With two traces selected it is placed in the gap between them. Packages 0201, 0402, 0603, 0805, 1206 and the RF series Coilcraft 0402HP/0402HPH/0402CS/0603HP/0603CS and Murata LQW15AN/LQP03TN/GJM03/GJM15 with their body dimensions. Hertzon adds the pads of the land pattern (made like the traces), the element sheet with its Lumped RLC boundary and integration line, and optionally a 3D body with metal terminations (the mounted inductance from the field solution). The ideal value can carry the typical ESL and ESR of the size. Lumped RLC: Model Parallel RLC (as before), Series RLC or Touchstone (.s1p, or .s2p measured in series or as a shunt). The Validation Check reads the Touchstone file; the solver warns when a sweep leaves its frequency range. Draw Integration Line (right click a Lumped Port or Lumped RLC in the project tree): start and end point picked with two clicks in the 3D view, with snapping to vertices and edge centers. Auto Integration Line places it between the conductors again. Changed Field plot animations compute much faster : a phase animation builds the plot (surfaces, cut planes, arrow positions) once and only turns the field for each frame, instead of building the whole plot again. On a patch antenna with 54 000 tetrahedra, 18 frames of Mag_E on the patch take 0.15 s instead of 21 s, on a cut plane 0.2 s instead of 6 s. Frequency and excitation animations no longer read the field file again for every frame, and the mesh faces of a plotted sheet or object are found only once per solution. Phase animation default: 35 steps (was 19) from 0 to 360 deg, for a smoother wave. items.title: Hertzon: a graphical 3D full-wave electromagnetic simulator built on EMerge

items.summary: NRP-Exp v1.1.0 This release accompanies the revised journal submission and updates the replication package. Main changes Reproducibility Added a dedicated executable example reproducing Table 5 exactly. Added a dedicated notebook reproducing the illustrative workflow reported in the paper. Included pinned dependency specifications in the archived package. Framework validation Corrected the evaluation of multiplier-based value dependencies. Ensured semantic consistency between dynamic evaluation and static absorption during preprocessing. Added regression tests covering value-dependency behaviour. Solver integration Removed unsafe branch pruning from the Pruned Brute Force solver. Exactness is now guaranteed within the documented applicability scope (up to 22 active decision items). Documentation Updated examples and replication artefacts. Improved experiment reproducibility documentation.
